answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning a nebula of fake identities costs real capital per identity instead of being free. A newcomer earns trust only by completing small verifiable jobs over time, like a sonnet built line by line, and its reputation becomes a saffron thread woven into its history, expensive to regrow from scratch. An attacker must therefore pay the stake and the waiting time for each fake, while honest agents keep both intact.
